title: Traditional Media
summary: Newspapers, magazines, radio and TV – why they still matter in a digital age.

reading.heading: What is Traditional Media?
reading.body: Traditional media refers to older, established forms of mass communication such as newspapers, magazines, radio, posters, billboards and broadcast television. These channels existed long before the internet and social media.
bullets: Traditional media includes print, outdoor adverts, radio and broadcast TV.
It is usually one-way communication with limited interactivity.
It can reach very large audiences but is often expensive.

reading.heading: Strengths and limitations
reading.body: Traditional media can still feel credible and reach large audiences, but it is usually less interactive and can cost more than digital channels.

questions.prompt: Define traditional media.
questions.hint: One clear sentence.

questions.prompt: State one traditional media format that could be used to promote a new theatre show.
questions.hint: Name one valid format.

questions.prompt: Explain one advantage of using a TV advert instead of a social media advert to promote a charity appeal.
questions.hint: Point + because/so.

questions.prompt: Describe two limitations of using posters instead of online adverts to target teenagers.
questions.hint: Two separate limitations with impact.

questions.prompt: Give one reason why traditional media is often combined with new media in modern campaigns.
questions.hint: Link the answer to audience reach or interaction.

title: New Media
summary: Websites, apps, streaming and social media – how digital technology changes the way media is delivered.

reading.heading: What is New Media?
reading.body: New media refers to digital forms of media that rely on computers, mobile devices and the internet. Examples include websites, social media platforms, video and music streaming services, podcasts, apps and online games.
bullets: Audiences can like, share, comment and create content.
Content can be highly targeted using user data and analytics.

reading.heading: New media in campaigns
reading.body: Advertisers use websites, social media, apps and video platforms because they allow targeting, fast distribution and two-way communication.
bullets: Websites and microsites hold detailed information and calls to action.
Social posts and stories support engagement.
Cross-platform campaigns combine web, social and offline media.

questions.prompt: State one example of new media.
questions.hint: Give a clear specific example.

questions.prompt: Explain one way that audiences can interact with new media.
questions.hint: Describe the interaction and the impact.

questions.prompt: Describe one advantage of using social media instead of posters to promote a new mobile game.
questions.hint: Targeting, interactivity or cost.

questions.prompt: Which is a feature of new media?
questions.hint: Choose the best answer.

questions.prompt: Why can new media be cheaper to distribute than traditional media?
questions.hint: Think about digital delivery.

title: Video, Audio & Music
summary: How moving image, sound and music are used to engage audiences and create meaning.

reading.heading: Video, audio and music in media products
reading.body: Video uses moving image, camerawork and editing. Audio covers dialogue, voiceover, sound effects and ambience. Music helps create mood and reinforce brand identity.
bullets: These elements work together to create meaning, mood and impact.
Dialogue and voiceover can inform or persuade.
Music and SFX can make content more memorable.

reading.heading: Working together
reading.body: A strong media product balances visuals, dialogue, sound effects and music so the audience clearly understands the message and feels the intended emotion.
bullets: Camera and editing affect pace and focus.
Mixing keeps dialogue clear over music and effects.
Silence can also create tension or focus.

questions.prompt: State one reason why music is used in a TV advert.
questions.hint: Short clear reason.

questions.prompt: Explain how sound effects can improve a gameplay trailer.
questions.hint: What do they add and what is the effect?

questions.prompt: Describe one way a voiceover can be used in a charity video.
questions.hint: Link tone or information to purpose and audience.

questions.prompt: Explain two ways camera shots and editing can be used together to create excitement in a sports highlight video.
questions.hint: Two linked points.

questions.prompt: Which element is most likely to set mood in a media product?
questions.hint: Choose the best answer.

title: Animation, SFX & VFX
summary: How movement, sound effects and visual effects bring media products to life.

reading.heading: Animation, SFX and VFX
reading.body: Animation creates movement frame-by-frame. SFX are audio clips that add realism or impact. VFX are visuals created or enhanced in software such as CGI or compositing.
bullets: Animation can be 2D, 3D, stop-motion or motion graphics.
VFX can create scenes that are dangerous, expensive or impossible to film.

reading.heading: Choosing techniques
reading.body: Effects should still match the message, budget and target audience of the media product.
bullets: Combining live action, VFX, SFX and music can increase impact.

questions.prompt: What does VFX stand for?
questions.hint: Use the full term.

questions.prompt: Explain one reason why a producer might use VFX instead of filming something for real.
questions.hint: Think about safety, cost or impossibility.

questions.prompt: Describe how sound effects can improve an action sequence.
questions.hint: What do they add?

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct?
questions.hint: Choose the best answer.
options: Animation creates moving images frame by frame
Animation cannot be used in adverts

questions.prompt: How can animation, SFX and VFX be combined in one media product?
questions.hint: Describe a sensible combination.

bullets: Focus: Staying safe on set and in the studio.
Use evidence from the topic page when answering.

reading.heading: Key things to remember
reading.body: The answers in this worksheet should stay close to the language and examples used in the live iMedia Genius page for Health & Safety.
bullets: Link each point to purpose, audience or suitability where relevant.

questions.hint: Use a key term from the reading.

questions.prompt: Explain one important feature of Health & Safety.
questions.hint: Make a point and develop it with why it matters.

questions.prompt: Which option is most closely linked to Health & Safety?
questions.hint: Choose the best match.

questions.prompt: Describe two points a student should remember about Health & Safety.
questions.hint: Give two separate ideas from the strand content.
